intervals.src: IPJ convention (ipj/src/ipj/rigor/bootstrap.py, trials.py): 95% percentile bootstrap over task clusters, 10,000 resamples, numpy default_rng(0); MC stream seed 20260711. Accuracy half-widths use the design effect 1.96*sqrt(p(1-p)(1+(k-1)rho)/(n k)), which matches a simulated percentile bootstrap to within 0.5 point (the simulated upper side is up to 0.5 wider at p=0.89, rho=0.8).

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next has no per-task vectors, so its chain takes the Qwen3.8-27B ratios.

s1_rule.src: author ruling 2026-09-25 ('local by default'): the deployed stage-1 threshold is the most accurate operating point of the headline plan whose owned cost is at least min_mult below the Fable 5.1 anchor and that keeps at least min_local_share of tasks finishing on the laptop (plan shares[0]). The false-escalation rate is swept in steps of fpr_step along the deployed signal's equal-variance binormal ROC at auc_combined_all (the construction of figures/fig_escalation_curves.py); stage 2 stays at s2_recall / s2_fpr; one threshold for every plan. The headline's first stage runs on a desk machine; of the two M5 Max configurations (candidates) the one whose rule-selected headline is more accurate is deployed for every Qwen3.8-27B-first plan. make_numbers.py re-runs the selection and fails if s1_recall, s1_fpr or the plans' machine drift from it. previous_point: recall / false escalation before round 15 Author ruling 2026-09-25 (round 17): the rule also caps the share of tasks sent to a closed-source provider at max_closed_share (at most 1 in 10), so the headline stays the three-stage system rather than a two-stage escalation straight to a closed-source model (about 25% of tasks).

signal.two_stage_solve_src: measured (round 25, author ruling 2026-09-25): the two-stage closed legs take P(solve | fired) on the E1 fired set, GPT-6 Astra 0.716 and GPT-5.6-sol 0.596 (targets were 0.65 and 0.63). Qwen3.8-27B -> GPT-5.6-sol then falls below the headline's accuracy, so 3.2's rented-basis pick at that accuracy is Qwen3.8-27B -> GPT-6 Astra. The three-stage legs keep their targets.

machine_model.note: Per attempt i of the 445 measured E1 attempts, scaled to AA's output tokens: t_dec = O/(r0*mtp*eff*f(D)), t_pre = U/(pp0/(1+D/dh)), t_tool measured, overhead measured; agent time capped at max(7200 s, task timeout); boundary energy = P_dec*t_dec + P_pre*t_pre + P_tool*(t_tool+t_over); wall energy per phase with each platform's own conversion. Every parameter: central c, range [min, max] for the projection Monte Carlo, and its source. Scratch prototype and full derivations: scratchpad/grounded/grounded_model.py.

c0_first_prompt.src: engineering estimate: uncached prefill per attempt U = 2*I/R - c0 (mean 28.1K scaled): Qwen3.x chat templates drop earlier turns' thinking, so the prefix cache holds up to the previous prompt and each turn prefills the previous visible reply plus the new observation; consistent with 1,149 read tokens per turn on the M4 Pro smoke run (EXP-20260921-01); c0 is the smallest E1 first prompts (2-request attempts start at about 1.5K). E1 records n_cache_tokens = 0, so the cached share is not measured

budget_floor_s.src: AA protocol: agent time <= max(7200 s, task timeout)

partial_solve_after_cut.src: measured: a cut attempt still passes with probability 11/136: E1 7/86 timed-out attempts, and the M4 Pro run (EXP-20260921-01 energy_87.json) 4 of its 50 graded AgentTimeoutError attempts. Round 10 used 11/113, counting only the M4 Pro timeouts on 900-s tasks (4/27), a subset with no stated reason

workload.scale_note: engineering estimate: output tokens, uncached tokens, prompt depth and tool time are scaled together by s = 67,549 / 84,017 (AA tokens / E1 mean); trial overhead (setup, verifier) is not scaled

depth_factor.src: measured: Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_XL llama-bench tg32 at depth on 2x RTX 3090 (llama.cpp #27623), 40.92 tok/s at 0. Machines differ around it: Spark NVFP4 0.948 @32K and 0.852 @100K (Kubesimplify; the curve gives 0.91 and 0.76), Strix Qwen3.6 Q8 0.94 @32K (kyuz0), M4 Max Qwen3.6 Q8+MTP 0.96 @32K (#29075) sit above it; M3 Ultra Q8_0+MTP 17.06/32.5 = 0.52 raw @89.6K, about 0.62 after its MTP acceptance drop (#29110; curve 0.78), and stared M5 Max Q8_0 17.0/18.4 = 0.924 @8K (curve 0.987) sit below it. The spread is carried by common.depth_gamma. Not applied to the batched datacenter rows, whose per-agent rates are in-campaign rates that already include depth

workload.tool_src: measured: E1 raw result.json, agent time minus summed request times (16.6 s per turn; GLM-5.3 rerun 16.3 s); Modal sandboxes rather than local Docker, difference unmeasured

mtp.src: CUDA and ROCm/Vulkan engines (DGX Spark vLLM, Strix Halo llama.cpp, H200 at one agent): measured batch-1 MTP speedups on Qwen3.6/3.8-27B: Spark vLLM 1.61-2.15 (NVIDIA forum study thread 381102, helge 380244), Strix llama.cpp 1.63-2.41 (Coffie 12.1 -> 21.2 tok/s at n=3; sudoingX). These are probe prompts: on CUDA the prose prompt gains 1.30-1.34x against 1.69-1.82x overall (sudoingX RTX 3090 control, same GGUF and build), and an agentic attempt is mostly reasoning prose, so the central sits at the low end of the measured cluster (engineering estimate). Round 10 also cited 'about 30% acceptance' from Kubesimplify; that figure is a DSpark k=7 drafter, not MTP, and is dropped

mtp_power.src: engineering estimate: decode power with MTP on CUDA/ROCm engines: Strix +1-2.5% (Beelink Qwen3.6 Q8 PPT 111.9-117.1 W without, 114.7-118.6 W with MTP); upper bound from Spark DSpark serving at 56-63 W against 43-45 W for plain dense decode

eff.src: measured, n = 1 task: M4 Pro decodes 10.6 tok/s inside a task against 13.0 tok/s at short context on the same machine and build (EXP-20260921-01 smoke); depth explains about 1% of the gap. Applied to every rate taken from a synthetic benchmark (desk machines, H200 with one agent)

weights_gb.src: GB read per decoded token, Qwen3.8-27B GGUF file sizes (Quesma): Q4_K_M 17.1 GB, Q8_0 29.0 GB. Round 10 used the Qwen3.6-27B Q4_K_M file (16,817,244,384 B, the IPJ M4 Pro GGUF). Q4_0 16.0 GB: Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 29.0 GB (Quesma) x the Unsloth Qwen3.8-27B Q4_0/Q8_0 size ratio 14.69/26.62 (ByteShape, 14 Sep 2026); cross-check Qwen3.6-27B Q4_0 16.1 GB (Quesma, 27 Jul 2026)

mtp_metal_kquant.src: Apple Metal llama.cpp with K-quants (the Q4_K_M Apple rows): MTP buys little. M3 Ultra 96 GB Q6_K: 22.8 -> 24.2 tok/s (+6.1%) at n-max 2 over mixed probe prompts, prose -11.8%, deeper drafts slower; Apple M4 Q3_K_XL: parity (-3.4% / +1.7%) (sudoingX/qwen38-mtp sweeps/apple-silicon.md). Quantized batch-8 decode amortizes 1.22x on Metal against 3.34x on CUDA, and K-quants reach the small-batch kernel only at ne11 >= 4 (same source); llama.cpp PR #29110's multi-column kernels cover Q4_0/Q8_0 only, the K-quant branch is #27776 (open). With MTP on, Metal prefill also slows (0.70-0.92x, stared M5 Max Q8_0). Central 1.0: MTP off, the configuration these measurements favour; the range allows MTP on at the measured mixed-probe gain and K-quant kernels landing (1.2, engineering estimate). Round 10 applied 1.6 here, from Q8_0 (#29110) and MLX (mlx-lm #990) measurements

mtp_power_metal_kquant.src: engineering estimate: decode power with MTP off (on: at most the Strix +2.5% at its cap)

mtp_metal_q8.src: Apple Metal llama.cpp Q8_0 (M5 Max 8-bit row): measured 1.56 (M3 Ultra, PR #29110 master at n_max 1: 34.2 llama-server against 21.91 batched-bench) and 1.68-1.78 (stared M5 Max: 31.7/18.4, 30.8/18.3, 31.5/17.7, 29.9/17.0 at 128/1K/4K/8K); lower end as for prose on CUDA (engineering estimate)

mtp_prefill_metal_q8.src: measured: prefill rate with MTP on over off, llama.cpp Metal Q8_0, stared M5 Max: 248/355, 470/628, 541/648, 521/567 at 128/1K/4K/8K (0.70-0.92, mean over 1K-8K 0.83)

depth_gamma.src: exponent on the measured depth curve, f(D)^gamma, carrying the spread across machines: gamma = ln(0.852)/ln(0.76) = 0.58 for the Spark at 100K and ln(0.62)/ln(0.78) = 1.9 for the M3 Ultra at 89.6K (workload.depth_factor)

kdram_inc.src: Apple DRAM power outside the powermetrics boundary, increment per GB/s of decode weight traffic: M4 Max Mac Studio RAM power rises from ~4 W to 15.7 W in decode (llama.cpp #22745, Stats.app, Gemma-4-31B Q8_0, about 32.9 GB of weights). The issue gives no decode rate: engineering estimate 12.5 tok/s [10, 14] (the M4 Pro's measured 79% of peak bandwidth on the M4 Max's 546 GB/s gives 13.1), i.e. 11.7 W over 411 GB/s. Traffic = r0 x eff x weight bytes (MTP does not raise weight reads)

dram_idle_w_per_gb.src: Apple DRAM idle power per GB of installed LPDDR: M1 Pro DRAM0 0.44 W for 16 GB (0.0275 W/GB); M4 Max RAM ~4 W for 128 GB before decode (#22745; 0.031 W/GB). Added in every phase on the Apple rows; on Strix Halo the idle DRAM is inside the platform term (Framework Desktop wall idle)

common.apple_cross_check: not applied: #22745 also reports Stats.app 'System Total' 109 W in decode and 145-152 W in prefill on a Mac Studio M4 Max (Apple support 102027 lists that machine's maximum as 145 W). The reported components (GPU 37 W, RAM 15.7 W) leave 56 W in decode unattributed, and the IPJ M4 Pro TerminalBench run measured 12.3 W for CPU and GPU together under llama.cpp, so a CPU draw of that size is not seen in our own runs; different model and format (Gemma-4-31B Q8_0, about 1.9x the bytes per token) and chassis. Unreconciled; if it transferred, the Apple wall conversion would be low by up to that amount

mtp_metal_q40.src: engineering estimate from the evidence behind mtp_metal_q8. llama.cpp PR #29110's multi-column Metal mat-vec kernels (ne11 = 2..8, the MTP verification batch) cover Q4_0 and Q8_0 only, so Q4_0 verifies drafts on the same fast path as Q8_0 (K-quants do not: mtp_metal_kquant). Measured Q8_0 MTP speedups on Metal: 1.56 (M3 Ultra, n_max 1, #29110) and 1.68-1.78 (stared M5 Max, n_max 3). For Q4_0, #29110's op-level timings at the 27B-class FFN shape (17408 x 5120, M3 Ultra) are 112.8 / 172.8 / 233.9 us at 2 / 3 / 4 columns, against about 106 us per matrix for one token of an in-model Q4_0 decode (21.91 x 29.0/16.0 x 0.742 = 29.5 tok/s on that chip): 1.06 / 1.63 / 2.21 decode steps, against 1.13 / 1.25 / 1.56 for Q8_0 model-level (#29110 batched-bench). With #29110's acceptance (0.891 at n_max 1, 0.836 at n_max 2) Q4_0's best depth is n_max 1 at about 1.78 before the draft head, Q8_0's n_max 2 at 2.02 (measured 2.03): ratio 0.88, so the Q8_0 central 1.6 becomes 1.41 on the M3 Ultra's kernel costs; central 1.5 because the M5 Max decodes Q4_0 nearer its bandwidth bound (7B Q4_0/Q8_0 efficiency 0.884 against the M3 Ultra's 0.742, #4167), leaving more compute for the extra columns. Range: 1.3 x 0.88 (rounded to 1.2) to the Q8_0 high end 1.75. Prefill with MTP on takes common.mtp_prefill_metal_q8 (measured on Q8_0; the draft head's prompt pass does not depend on the weight format), decode power common.mtp_power

Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M mean KLD 0.014 (Quesma, 26 Aug 2026); Quesma did not measure Q4_0 on Qwen3.8, so it is scaled by the Qwen3.6-27B ratio Q4_0/Q4_K_M = 0.035/0.017 = 2.06 (Quesma, 27 Jul 2026) to 0.029; at the Qwen3.8 TB2.1 dose-response slope of -85 points per nat (2-bit: 57 vs 63 of 89 at KLD 0.079), -85 x (0.029 - 0.014) = -1.3 points beyond Q4_K_M, i.e. -2.3 against BF16. signal.note: auc_deployed: errors, time budget and the owned GLM-5.3 trace judge on GAIA (engineering estimate: above the measured error/time-budget/loop flags, 0.549 on Qwen3.6-27B over 165 tasks; at the low end of published trajectory-reading calibrators on GAIA, 0.607-0.686, HTC arXiv 2601.15778 Table 3). auc_flags: the measured 0.549, carried like errored_fire_pct_measured. auc_answer_judge: the stretch sheet's answer-reading gate (GAIA_final plan 6), kept for record; no costed plan uses it. s2_*: GAIA_final plan 6 (chain) and plan 14 (GLM-first) operating points at s2_auc.

model.note: GAIA plan model (make_numbers.gaia_plan), the TB2.1 plan() structure with GAIA primitives. Under a near-random stage-1 signal the escalated tasks are a near-random sample, so GLM-5.3's solve rates on them are its marginal rates: glm_solve_false_esc = P(GLM | Qwen solved), measured 98/109 (Qwen3.6-27B vs GLM-5.3, 165 tasks, EXP-20260803-02 gaia_composed_corrected.json); P(GLM | Qwen failed) is derived from the tier accuracies. Astra's rates are those of the GLM-5.3 -> GPT-6 Astra plan (GAIA_final plan 14), which the chain becomes at 100% escalation. Costs and judge as GAIA_final plan 6 (GLM premium 1.5, Astra premium constants.premium). e1_cap: at most 35% of tasks leave the local stage. The local stage (gaia.tiers.qwen38) is the stretch desk build of GAIA_final: M5 Max 128 GB, Q4/NVFP4 + MTP, 13 kJ at the wall, rented = amortized desk basis.

redistribution.note: GLM-5.3 -> GPT-6 Astra at capability targets of 90% and 80% of GPT-6 Astra's accuracy (author note, 2026-09-25). The GLM-5.3 gate is a binormal ROC fitted to the stored glmfirst plan (it escalates 15.0% of GLM's correct answers and 81.8% of its failures); Astra's success on escalated GLM-correct and GLM-failed tasks is solved from that plan and Astra's leaderboard accuracy. The operating point is the smallest whole number of escalated attempts over 66 tasks x 5 rolls that reaches the target; the Astra leg keeps the stored plan's per-basis escalation premium. No TB4 run of GLM-5.3 or Astra exists (targets/STATUS.md).

evidence_gaps.note: Round 23 (2026-09-25): patterns the too-clean audit found where no evidence exists to give each entity its own input. Each is left as is and listed here.
evidence_gaps.machine_intervals: Table 3's kJ-per-solved intervals are 22 to 26% of their points for every machine: one workload profile (the 445 E1 attempts), one bootstrap index set and one correlation (0.65). No per-machine run exists.
evidence_gaps.desk_budget_cuts: M5 Max (Q4_K_M) and M3 Ultra decode at 27.4 and 27.6 tok/s from separate sources, so the hard time budget cuts the same attempts of the one workload profile and their accuracies tie. No agentic run on either machine exists.
evidence_gaps.flashnext_profile: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next runs on Qwen3.8-27B's E1 token, time and solve profile; its token counts are unpublished.
evidence_gaps.gaia_swe_premiums: GAIA and SWE-bench Verified escalated legs use the legacy single premium (1.93) or 1.5; no per-task costs exist on either benchmark.
evidence_gaps.tb4_localfirst_tie: Terminal-Bench 4.0 local-first and open-weight first share the Astra premium and conditionals of the target sheet; only the Qwen3.6 proxy (0 of 63) exists.
evidence_gaps.shared_stage1_threshold: Every Qwen3.8-27B-first plan uses the one deployed stage-1 threshold, so they share a fire rate and local share. This is the deployed design, not a missing measurement.
evidence_gaps.glm_gate: GLM-5.3's escalation gate (recall 0.70, false escalation 0.05) is one target shared by every plan that runs through GLM-5.3; it awaits the GLM-5.3 gate experiment (author ruling 2026-09-25: keep the shared target).
evidence_gaps.judge_auc_structure: Measured on the 445 E1 attempts (gpt-5-mini judge): flags 0.731, judge on all attempts 0.795, judge on completed attempts 0.618. The targets (0.74 / 0.89 / 0.88) assume the judge holds up on completed attempts (author ruling 2026-09-25: keep the targets, no change in the paper).
